newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania moves to curb money-laundering.
newsitem.headline: Romania moves to curb money-laundering.

text.p: Romania, which has seen a surge in organised crime in the post-communist era, has issued draft rules to curb laundering of money from illegal traffic in drugs, weapons, nuclear material, gambling and prostitution.
A bill adopted by the cabinet late on Saturday makes money-laundering through the Balkan state's banking and financial institutions a crime punishable with jail terms of up to 12 years.

The law, to be submitted for parliament's approval, plans the creation of a money-laundering watchdog, including experts from the interior and finance ministries and from Romania's National (central) Bank.

The watchdogs will monitor money-laundering through potential outlets including commercial, investment or savings banks, pension and credit funds, brokerage houses, licensed money exchange bureaux and the insurance sector.
"This draft law aligns Romania to European standards in fighting money-laundering practices," a senior interior ministry official, Colonel Radu Olteanu, told reporters.
Casinos, which have mushroomed across Romania since gambling was made legal after the 1989 fall of communism, will also come under the watchdogs' scrutiny, Olteanu said.
Romanian police had complained about existing legal loopholes which allowed crimes such as money laundering to go unpunished until now.
The move is part of a tough campaign launched by the centrists, who ousted the communists in elections last November, to fight corruption and organised crime.
In recent years Romania has become a conduit for drugs, weapons and even nuclear material smuggled in from the Middle East or the former Soviet Union, and bound for markets in the West.
Romanian police have reported a surge in trafficking of radioactive substances, mainly uranium from Ukraine, but amounts in most cases have been small, and not of weapons-grade material.
